name: piix4_setup
prose: Precondition: PIIX4_dev is a valid PCI device for a PIIX4-class SMBus controller whose config space can be accessed; if the module parameter force_addr is nonzero it is a usable SMBus base address. Postcondition: it sets the global srvrworks_csb5_delay to 1 for a ServerWorks CSB5, then returns -EPERM (with an error message) if dmi_check_system(piix4_dmi_blacklist) matches or if dmi_check_system(piix4_dmi_ibm) matches and the device vendor is Intel. It then takes the base address from force_addr (masked with 0xfff0, and clears the module parameter force) or reads SMBBA from config space and returns -ENODEV if that is 0; returns -ENODEV if acpi_check_region fails and -EBUSY if request_region of the SMBIOSIZE-byte region fails. If force_addr is set it disables the controller, programs the new base address and re-enables it; otherwise, if the host controller is disabled and force is set it force-enables it, and if force is not set it releases the region and returns -ENODEV. On success it returns the 16-bit-aligned nonzero base address with the I/O region still requested for the caller to release; every failure return after request_region (only the disabled-controller one) releases it first. Config-space read/write return codes are ignored.
note: reviewer (round 15) is wrong: the DMI blacklist and IBM -EPERM checks are in piix4_setup itself (i2c-piix4.c piix4_setup), not only in probe. Slice cut the head (name outside slice, function starts at i2c-piix4.c:225). Old prose omitted srvrworks_csb5_delay and the clearing of 'force'.

name: rk3x_i2c_v1_calc_timings
prose: Precondition: clk_rate is nonzero and t and t_calc point to valid structures. Postcondition: if t->bus_freq_hz is above I2C_MAX_FAST_MODE_PLUS_FREQ or below 1000 it WARNs and clamps it into that range. It then computes the low and high divider counts from the spec timings for that bus frequency (rk3x_i2c_get_spec), the SCL rise and fall times and clk_rate, picks the SDA-update, start-setup and stop-setup configuration fields, stores the packed fields in t_calc->tuning, decrements t_calc->div_low and t_calc->div_high by one, clamps each to 0xffff and returns -EINVAL if either was clamped, otherwise 0. t_calc->div_low, div_high and tuning are always written; it takes no lock and holds no reference.
note: slice cut the head: packet name rk3x_i2c_calc_timings does not exist; the function whose tail is in the slice is rk3x_i2c_v1_calc_timings (i2c-rk3x.c:744-872). Prose kept from the previous round, which matched the code.

name: sh_mobile_i2c_isr_rx
prose: Precondition: pd and pd->msg are valid, pd->pos is at least -1, and pd->msg->len + 2 is representable as int. Postcondition: it computes real_pos = pd->pos - 2 and acts on the first matching case: pos == -1 issues i2c_op(OP_TX_FIRST); pos == 0 issues OP_TX_TO_RX; pos == msg->len with stop_after_dma set issues OP_RX_STOP, stores no byte, and increments pd->pos twice in total (once in the branch and once at the done label); pos == msg->len without stop_after_dma issues OP_RX_STOP when real_pos < 0, otherwise stores the result of OP_RX_STOP_DATA in msg->buf[real_pos]; otherwise, when real_pos >= 0, it stores the result of OP_RX in msg->buf[real_pos]; otherwise (for example pos == 1 with msg->len != 1) it performs no operation. In every case other than the stop_after_dma branch pd->pos is incremented once. It returns 1 if the new pd->pos equals msg->len + 2 and 0 otherwise.
note: reviewers rounds 2 and 15 right: the stop_after_dma branch increments pos by 2, and for pos == 1 with msg->len == 1 an OP_RX_STOP is issued (old 'no operation when pos == 1' was imprecise). i2c-sh_mobile.c:371-385.

name: i2c_acpi_get_info
prose: Precondition: adev is a valid ACPI device, info points to a writable struct i2c_board_info, adapter is NULL or an i2c_adapter, and adapter_handle is NULL or points to writable storage. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if adev is already enumerated; otherwise it calls i2c_acpi_do_lookup and returns its nonzero result, which is -EINVAL when acpi_bus_get_status fails, when resource retrieval fails or no I2cSerialBus slave address is found, and -ENODEV when the device is not ready for enumeration or matches the ignored-device id list (after the ready and ignored-id checks the lookup has already zeroed *info and may have filled part of it). If adapter is non-NULL it returns -ENODEV when device_match_acpi_handle(&adapter->dev, lookup.adapter_handle) is false; if adapter is NULL it returns -ENODEV when the adapter's ACPI device cannot be found, its status cannot be read or it is not present. Otherwise it sets info->fwnode, stores lookup.adapter_handle in *adapter_handle when that pointer is non-NULL, fills info->type with acpi_set_modalias and returns 0. It takes no lock and holds no reference after return.
note: reviewers right: a missing I2cSerialBus resource returns -EINVAL (not -ENOENT, last check in i2c_acpi_do_lookup), -ENODEV comes from the ready/ignored-id checks, and lookup failure maps to -EINVAL/-ENODEV only; old prose invented -ENOENT. i2c-core-acpi.c:232-337 and i2c_acpi_do_lookup at 145-174.

name: i2c_acpi_space_handler
prose: Precondition: handler_context points to an i2c_acpi_handler_data whose adapter is valid and whose info.connection/info.length describe an ACPI resource buffer; function carries the accessor type in bits 16 and above and the ACPI_READ/ACPI_WRITE action in the low bits; value64 is NULL or a gsb_buffer the handler may read and write. Postcondition: it returns the acpi_status of acpi_buffer_to_resource without allocating anything if the conversion fails. Otherwise it allocates a temporary i2c_client (AE_NO_MEMORY on failure), returns AE_BAD_PARAMETER if value64 is NULL or the resource is not an I2cSerialBus one or the accessor type is not SEND_RCV, BYTE, WORD, BLOCK or MULTIBYTE (the unsupported-accessor case also logs a warning), and in those AE_BAD_PARAMETER and AE_NO_MEMORY cases gsb->status is not written. For a supported accessor it performs the SMBus (or, for MULTIBYTE, raw i2c_transfer based) read or write at the resource's slave address, copies read data into the gsb buffer on success, stores the helper's status in gsb->status (0 on success, a negative errno, or the helper's positive AE_NO_MEMORY from the MULTIBYTE helpers) and returns AE_OK. The temporary client and the converted resource are freed on every path after the conversion succeeds.
note: reviewers rounds 2 and 15 wrong: code returns AE_BAD_PARAMETER for an unsupported accessor (default case of the accessor switch in i2c_acpi_space_handler) and does store status in gsb->status. Prose kept with the early-return details added.

name: i3c_master_setda_locked
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the master's bus lock (this is the _locked variant) and master is valid; oldaddr and newaddr are u8 values and setdasa selects the CCC. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL without allocating or sending anything if oldaddr or newaddr is 0; it returns -ENOMEM without sending anything if i3c_ccc_cmd_dest_init fails; otherwise it stores newaddr << 1 in the SETDA payload, builds a SETDASA (setdasa true) or SETNEWDA (setdasa false) CCC addressed to oldaddr, sends it with i3c_master_send_ccc_cmd_locked, cleans up the destination, and returns the result of the send. The destination is cleaned up on every path after it is successfully initialised, and no memory is retained.
note: reviewers' complaints were about the formal contract only (it was weaker than the prose and mentioned lock); contract dropped because the function performs bus I/O. i3c/master.c:1268-1291.

name: i3c_master_setdasa_locked
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the master's bus lock and master is valid; static_addr and dyn_addr are u8 values. Postcondition: it returns i3c_master_setda_locked(master, static_addr, dyn_addr, true) unchanged: -EINVAL if either address is 0, -ENOMEM if the CCC destination cannot be initialised, otherwise the result of sending the locked SETDASA CCC (0 or a negative errno).
note: thin wrapper (i3c/master.c:1293-1297). Contract dropped (bus I/O); reviewer comments were about the contract only.

name: i3c_master_setnewda_locked
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the master's bus lock and master is valid; oldaddr and newaddr are u8 values. Postcondition: it returns i3c_master_setda_locked(master, oldaddr, newaddr, false) unchanged: -EINVAL if either address is 0, -ENOMEM if the CCC destination cannot be initialised, otherwise the result of sending the locked SETNEWDA CCC (0 or a negative errno).
note: thin wrapper (i3c/master.c:1299-1303). Contract dropped (bus I/O).

name: dw_i3c_master_end_xfer_locked
prose: Precondition: the caller holds master->xferqueue.lock; master->xferqueue.cur may be NULL; the response count read from the hardware and the TIDs in the responses index into the current transfer's cmds array; isr is not used. Postcondition: if master->xferqueue.cur is NULL it returns at once. Otherwise it reads the response count from QUEUE_STATUS_LEVEL, then for each of those responses reads RESPONSE_QUEUE_PORT, stores the data length in cmd->rx_len and the error status in cmd->error of cmds[TID], and reads rx_len bytes from the RX FIFO into that command's rx_buf when the length is nonzero and the error is 0. It then scans the error fields of cmds[0..nresp-1] and sets ret to 0, or to the code for the last non-zero error seen (-EIO for parity, IBA NACK, transfer abort, CRC and frame errors; -ENOSPC for over/underflow; -EINVAL for I2C write NACK, address NACK and any unknown value), stores it in xfer->ret and calls complete(&xfer->comp). If ret is negative it calls dw_i3c_master_dequeue_xfer_locked and sets DEV_CTRL_RESUME in DEVICE_CTRL. Finally it takes the first entry of master->xferqueue.list (removing it from the list) as the new master->xferqueue.cur, which is NULL when the list is empty, and calls dw_i3c_master_start_xfer_locked. It returns nothing.
note: reviewer (round 15) is wrong: cur is set to the first list entry or NULL when the list is empty (master->xferqueue.cur = xfer after list_first_entry_or_null). Round 1/2 comments (only nresp commands are filled/checked) are already reflected in the prose.

name: adxl345_set_act_inact_ac
prose: Precondition: st is an initialised adxl345_state with a valid regmap and type is a valid adxl345_activity_type index into adxl345_act_acdc_msk. Postcondition: it computes a boolean that is true only when type is ADXL345_ACTIVITY_AC or ADXL345_INACTIVITY_AC and cmd_en is true (the other branch computes ADXL345_COUPLING_DC && cmd_en, which is always false because ADXL345_COUPLING_DC is 0), and calls regmap_assign_bits on ADXL345_REG_ACT_INACT_CTRL with the mask adxl345_act_acdc_msk[type]: the mask bits are set when that boolean is true and cleared otherwise. It returns the result of that regmap call, 0 on success or a negative errno.
note: reviewers (rounds 1 and 15) are wrong: regmap_assign_bits takes a bool value (regmap.h:1397-1404), so the 0/1 produced by && sets or clears the mask bits as the old prose said. Prose clarified that non-AC types always clear the bit.

name: ab8500_gpadc_read
prose: Precondition: gpadc is NULL or an initialised ab8500_gpadc, ch describes a channel, ibat is NULL or points to an int, and the caller has re-armed gpadc->complete for the conversion (the function waits on it but does not reinitialise it). Postcondition: it returns -ENODEV if gpadc is NULL and -ENOTSUPP if the needed software or hardware interrupt (irq_sw or irq_hw) is not set up for the channel, before touching the PM state. Otherwise it calls pm_runtime_get_sync (result ignored), polls the GPADC status register up to 10 times at 20 ms intervals for the busy bit to clear (returning -EINVAL if it stays busy), programs the average-sample and control registers, starts a software conversion or sets the trigger timer for hardware control, waits for completion (2 s for hardware control, AB8500_GPADC_CONVERSION_TIME ms otherwise) and returns -EINVAL on timeout, then reads the low and high data registers. For the four double-conversion channels it returns -ENOTSUPP for hardware control, otherwise reads the second conversion and stores it in *ibat when ibat is non-NULL (a warning only if NULL). It then writes the disable value to CTRL1; on success it calls pm_runtime_put_autosuspend and returns (high_data << 8) | low_data. Any register error, timeout or -ENOTSUPP after the PM get jumps to a common exit that attempts to disable the GPADC again (result ignored), calls pm_runtime_put and returns the negative errno; *ibat may already have been written if the failure was the final disable write.
note: slice cut the head; packet name ab8500_gpadc_conversion does not exist, the function is ab8500_gpadc_read (ab8500-gpadc.c:386-628). Old prose wrongly said the caller holds a PM reference (the function takes it with pm_runtime_get_sync), missed the -ENODEV/-ENOTSUPP early returns and the busy -EINVAL, and wrongly said *ibat is never modified on failure.

name: ad4130_write_channel_setup
prose: Precondition: st is an initialised ad4130_state and channel is a valid index into st->chans_info. Postcondition: it returns 0 without changes when on_enable is true and the channel is already linked to a slot. When on_enable is false and the channel is not enabled it unlinks the channel from its slot if it has one (ad4130_unlink_channel) and returns 0. Otherwise it calls ad4130_find_slot and returns its nonzero error if no slot is found; unlinks the channel from its current slot if linked; if the chosen slot must be overwritten it calls ad4130_unlink_slot (which in the code shown always returns 0) and ad4130_write_slot_setup, returning the latter's error; and finally returns the result of ad4130_link_channel_slot. On an error return the channel may already have been unlinked and the slot's setup may be partly written; channels that are disabled and unlinked stay unlinked.
note: reviewer (round 15) is right: ad4130_unlink_slot cannot return an error (ad4130.c:678-692, return 0), so 'regmap error from ad4130_unlink_slot' in the old prose was wrong; the 'ret = ad4130_unlink_slot(...)' check is dead code.

name: ad4695_osr_to_regval
prose: Precondition: ratio may be any int. Postcondition: it scans the static table ad4695_oversampling_ratios (1, 4, 16, 64) in order and returns the index of the first entry equal to ratio, i.e. 0, 1, 2 or 3 for ratio 1, 4, 16 or 64, and returns -EINVAL for any other ratio; it has no side effects.
note: ad4695.c:584-596; table at line 404. Contract dropped: it was repeatedly rejected for omitting the EINVAL name though correct.

name: mcp320x_channel_to_tx_data
prose: Precondition: channel is at most 7 and differential is false or true. Postcondition: for device_index mcp3002 or mcp3202 it returns the bitwise OR (1 << 4) | (!differential << 3) | (channel << 2); for mcp3004, mcp3204, mcp3008 or mcp3208 it returns (1 << 6) | (!differential << 5) | (channel << 2); for any other device_index it returns -EINVAL. Because these are ORs rather than sums, the first group's result equals 16 + (differential ? 0 : 8) + 4*channel only when channel is 0 or 1. It reads no global state and has no side effects.
contract: /*@ requires channel <= 7; ensures ((device_index == 1 || device_index == 5) ==> result == (16 | (differential ? 0 : 8) | (channel << 2))) && ((device_index == 2 || device_index == 3 || device_index == 6 || device_index == 7) ==> result == (64 | (differential ? 0 : 32) | (channel << 2))) && ((device_index != 1 && device_index != 5 && device_index != 2 && device_index != 3 && device_index != 6 && device_index != 7) ==> result == -22); */
note: mcp320x.c:99-119. The old prose said the results are sums, which is wrong for channel >= 2 in the 16-bit-start group (bit overlap); corrected contract uses the enum values mcp3002=1, mcp3004=2, mcp3008=3, mcp3202=5, mcp3204=6, mcp3208=7.

name: _get_gpio_reg
prose: Precondition: when offset is at most 31, base is at least offset / 8 and base - offset / 8 fits in int. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if offset is greater than 31; otherwise it returns base - offset / 8, computed in unsigned arithmetic and converted to int. It has no side effects.
note: rohm-bd79112.c:154-160. Prose was right; contract dropped because the previous contract kept failing the mechanical EINVAL check.

name: ccs811_probe
prose: Precondition: client is a valid i2c_client. Postcondition: it returns -EOPNOTSUPP if the adapter lacks the needed SMBus functionality, -ENOMEM if devm_iio_device_alloc fails, and PTR_ERR of the wakeup GPIO if devm_gpiod_get_optional fails, all before ccs811_set_wakeup is called. It then sets the client's driver data, raises the wakeup line, and returns, after lowering it again, the error from ccs811_reset, from either register read (negative), -ENODEV on a wrong hardware id or hardware version, or the negative result of ccs811_setup. After a successful setup it lowers the wakeup line, initialises the mutex and fills in name, info, mode and channels. If client->irq > 0 it requests a threaded IRQ, allocates, configures and registers a data-ready trigger and takes a reference to it; any failure of those steps goes to the err_poweroff exit. It then calls iio_triggered_buffer_setup (failure undoes the trigger registration if one was made and goes to err_poweroff) and iio_device_register (failure also cleans up the triggered buffer). All three error exits write CCS811_MEAS_MODE idle (result ignored) and return the stored errno. It returns 0 on success.
note: reviewers right: the old prose said iio_triggered_buffer_setup/iio_device_register are always called, but an IRQ/trigger failure skips them (ccs811_probe, if (client->irq > 0) block followed by iio_triggered_buffer_setup). The round-2 'reset GPIO' complaint is wrong: there is no reset GPIO here, reset is an I2C write in ccs811_reset.

name: sgp40_exp
prose: Precondition: exp is not INT_MIN; power is at most 30 (and at most 15 when exp < 0, since 1 << (power * 2) is evaluated); rounds is at most 33 so factorial does not wrap to zero; and every shift count xp >> divider stays below 32 (guaranteed for example when power * rounds <= 31, but also kept small by the xp >= xmax reduction step, which is what makes calls with larger products such as power 14 and rounds 18 work). Postcondition: it returns 1 << power when exp is 0. Otherwise, with x = |exp|, it runs a fixed-point Taylor series over the given number of rounds in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic (xp, factorial and y may wrap) giving y, an approximation of 2^power * e^(x / 2^power), and returns y for exp > 0 or (1 << (power * 2)) / y for exp < 0 (y must be nonzero). It has no side effects.
note: reviewer (round 15) right that power*rounds <= 31 is not satisfied by the real caller (power 14, rounds 18); that was a sufficient condition for the shift not being too large, the real requirement is that divider stays below 32. sgp40.c:106-136.

name: ssp_enable_mcu
prose: Precondition: data points to an initialised ssp_data whose spi and spi->irq are valid. Postcondition: it returns nothing; it logs the old and requested shutdown state with dev_info, then if enable is true and data->shut_down is true it sets data->shut_down to false and calls enable_irq and enable_irq_wake on data->spi->irq; if enable is false and data->shut_down is false it sets data->shut_down to true and calls disable_irq and disable_irq_wake; in the other two cases it only logs a warning. In every case data->shut_down equals !enable when the function returns.
note: reviewer (round 15) is right: the old prose said shut_down ends as !enable only when a transition occurred, but in the two no-op cases shut_down already equals !enable, so it holds after every call (ssp_dev.c:92-108).

name: ad5421_write_unlocked
prose: Precondition: the caller holds st->lock (ad5421_write takes it; this function does not), because it uses the shared st->data[0] DMA buffer. Postcondition: it stores cpu_to_be32((reg << 16) | val) in st->data[0].d32 and sends the three bytes d8[1..3] with spi_write, so the transmitted 24-bit word is ((reg << 16) | val) & 0xffffff, big-endian: bits 8 and higher of reg beyond the low 8 are dropped, but bits 16 to 23 of val, if set, are ORed into the register byte. It returns the result of spi_write, 0 on success or a negative errno.
note: reviewer (round 15) is right: val bits 16-23 are not discarded, they OR into the transmitted reg byte (ad5421.c:134-142); old prose said only the low 16 bits of val are sent.

name: ad5592r_write_raw_get_fmt
prose: Precondition: none; indio_dev and chan are not used. Postcondition: it returns IIO_VAL_INT_PLUS_NANO (3) when mask equals IIO_CHAN_INFO_SCALE (2 in enum iio_chan_info_enum) and IIO_VAL_INT_PLUS_MICRO (2) for every other mask; the final return -EINVAL is unreachable. It has no side effects.
note: old prose said IIO_CHAN_INFO_SCALE is 1; the enum (include/linux/iio/types.h:41-44) makes it 2. Reviewers: round 2's 'scale is 1' and round 15's 'NANO is 2, MICRO is 1' are wrong (NANO=3, MICRO=2, types.h:27-28); round 1 right that the contract encoded wrong constants.

name: iio_dummy_evgen_create
prose: Precondition: runs once at module init with the global pointer iio_evgen not yet allocated. Postcondition: it allocates iio_evgen with kzalloc and returns -ENOMEM if that fails (iio_evgen then stays NULL). Otherwise it creates the simulated IRQ domain for IIO_EVENTGEN_NO interrupts; if irq_domain_create_sim returns an error pointer it frees iio_evgen with kfree and returns that error, leaving the global iio_evgen non-NULL but pointing to freed memory. On success it initialises iio_evgen->lock and returns 0.
note: iio_dummy_evgen.c:46-64; reviewer comments were about the contract only (contract dropped: global state).

name: iio_dummy_evgen_get_irq
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition: it returns -ENODEV if iio_evgen is NULL. Otherwise, under iio_evgen->lock, it finds the first of the IIO_EVENTGEN_NO (10) slots whose inuse flag is clear, calls irq_create_mapping on the simulated domain for that slot, and marks the slot in use whether or not the mapping call returned a valid irq; it returns -ENOMEM if all slots are already in use and otherwise returns the value from irq_create_mapping (the Linux irq number, or 0 if the mapping failed). The caller is expected to release the irq with iio_dummy_evgen_release_irq.
note: iio_dummy_evgen.c:67-90; the old 'non-negative irq number' hid that a failed mapping returns 0 but the slot is still marked in use. Contract dropped (global state).

name: iio_dummy_evgen_init
prose: Precondition: runs at module init with the evgen not yet created. Postcondition: it calls iio_dummy_evgen_create and returns its negative error if that fails. Otherwise it initialises iio_evgen_dev, names it iio_evgen and calls device_add; if device_add fails it calls put_device on the device and returns the error from device_add, otherwise it returns 0.
note: iio_dummy_evgen.c:197-208. Prose of the previous round was right; contract dropped (global state), the reviewer comments were about the contract only.

name: adf4371_pll_fract_n_compute
prose: Precondition: pfd is nonzero and fits in 32 bits, vco / pfd fits in 32 bits, and integer, fract1, fract2 and mod2 point to writable unsigned ints. Postcondition: it returns nothing. It stores *integer = vco / pfd and *fract1 = ((vco % pfd) * ADF4371_MODULUS1) / pfd (ADF4371_MODULUS1 = 2^25), sets *fract2 = ((vco % pfd) * 2^25) % pfd and *mod2 = pfd, then while *mod2 is greater than ADF4371_MAX_MODULUS2 (BIT(14) = 16384) it right-shifts both *mod2 and *fract2 by one, and finally divides both by gcd(*fract2, *mod2). On return *mod2 is at most 16384 and *fract2 is at most *mod2; *fract2 can equal *mod2 (both then reduce to 1) because the halving rounds down independently. It takes no lock and the caller keeps ownership of all memory.
note: reviewer (round 15) is right: fract2 < mod2 is not guaranteed once both are halved (e.g. odd mod2 with fract2 = mod2 - 1 gives equal values, adf4371.c:219-243); old prose claimed 0 <= fract2 < mod2. Round 2's 2^14 = 32768 claim is wrong (BIT(14) = 16384).

name: bmg160_convert_freq_to_bit
prose: Precondition: none; val may be any int. Postcondition: it scans bmg160_samp_freq_table in order and returns the bw_bits of the first row whose odr equals val: 7 for 100, 6 for 200, 3 for 400, 2 for 1000 and 1 for 2000 (the later table rows with odr 100 and 200 are never reached); it returns -EINVAL for any other val. It has no side effects.
note: bmg160_core.c:121-127 and 152-161. Contract dropped: it was repeatedly rejected by the mechanical EINVAL check though correct.

name: AFE440X_TABLE_ATTR(_name, _table)
prose: Generated function _name_show(dev, attr, buf), defined together with a read-only DEVICE_ATTR by the AFE440X_TABLE_ATTR macro. Precondition: buf is a writable page-sized (PAGE_SIZE) sysfs buffer and _table is an array of struct afe440x_val_table with at least one entry (with zero entries buf[len - 1] would be buf[-1]). Postcondition: for each table entry in order it appends the text "%d.%06u " (integer, then fract zero-padded to six digits, then a space) with scnprintf, which never writes past PAGE_SIZE and truncates the output if it does not fit; it then replaces the last character written with a newline and returns the number of bytes written. It takes no lock and holds no references.
note: macro-generated at afe440x.h:117-132. Reviewer (round 15) partly right: scnprintf bounds the output to PAGE_SIZE - 1 characters, so the old precondition about fit was about truncation, not overflow; also the format zero-pads fract to 6 digits (old prose omitted it) and an empty table is out of bounds.

name: inv_icm42600_set_pwr_mgmt0
prose: Precondition: st is an initialised inv_icm42600_state; gyro and accel are sensor modes, temp says whether temperature is enabled; sleep_ms is NULL or points to an unsigned int. Postcondition: if the requested gyro, accel and temp are all equal to the current st->conf values it returns 0 without any write. Otherwise it writes the PWR_MGMT0 register with regmap_write and returns the error if that fails (st->conf unchanged). On success it updates st->conf.gyro.mode, accel.mode and temp_en, computes the longest needed settling time among: temperature turn-on, accel start from OFF, gyro start from OFF and gyro stop to OFF (waiting 200-300 microseconds with usleep_range for the accel and gyro start cases), and then either stores it in *sleep_ms when sleep_ms is non-NULL or msleeps for it when it is nonzero. It returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; real name inv_icm42600_set_pwr_mgmt0 (inv_icm42600_core.c:227-290). The earlier drop was wrong: the function exists in the file; the dropped prose also omitted the regmap_write error return.

name: inv_mpu_probe
prose: Precondition: client is a valid i2c_client being probed. Postcondition: it returns -EOPNOTSUPP if the adapter lacks I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_I2C_BLOCK, -ENOSYS if neither device_get_match_data nor the i2c id identifies the chip, PTR_ERR of the regmap if devm_regmap_init_i2c fails, and the negative result of inv_mpu_core_probe if that fails. If inv_mpu_i2c_aux_bus() is true it then allocates a mux with i2c_mux_alloc and stores it in st->muxc (returning -ENOMEM on failure), sets st->muxc->priv, and calls i2c_mux_add_adapter, returning its error directly (no mux adapter has been added in that case); then it calls inv_mpu_acpi_create_mux_client and, if that fails, calls i2c_mux_del_adapters on st->muxc and returns its error. It returns 0 otherwise, including when the aux bus is not used.
note: reviewers rounds 2 and 15 right: i2c_mux_add_adapter failure returns without deleting adapters because none was added (inv_mpu_i2c.c:93-142); old wording 'already-added mux adapter' and 'inv_mpu_remove later releases' removed as unverified.

name: smi240_sensor_data_is_valid
prose: Precondition: none; data may be any u32. Postcondition: it returns false if smi240_crc3(data, SMI240_CRC_INIT (0x05), SMI240_CRC_POLY (0x0B)) is nonzero, and false if both the SD bit (bit 31) and the CS bit (bit 3) of data are set; otherwise it returns true. It has no side effects.
note: smi240.c:170-181. Contract dropped: the previous giant xor expansion of the CRC kept failing syntax checks and cannot be verified.

name: opt4060_als_time_to_index
prose: Precondition: none; als_integration_time may be any u32. Postcondition: it scans the second column of opt4060_int_time_available (600, 1000, 1800, 3400, 6500, 12700, 25000, 50000, 100000, 200000, 400000, 800000) in order and returns the row index (0 to 11) of the first entry equal to als_integration_time, or -EINVAL if there is none. It has no side effects.
note: opt4060.c:153-167 and 187-197. Contract dropped: the previous version was rejected by the mechanical EINVAL check although correct.

name: gain_mul_div_helper
prose: Precondition: gain is at most 4096, div is nonzero and at least gain (so that no intermediate u64 value overflows). Postcondition: if val is less than GENMASK_ULL(51, 0) (2^52 - 1) it computes val * gain first and then divides by div with do_div, otherwise it divides first and multiplies by gain afterwards; the returned u64 is floor(val * gain / div) in the first case and floor(val / div) * gain in the second. It has no side effects.
contract: /*@ requires gain <= 4096 && div > 0 && div >= gain; ensures (val < 4503599627370495 ==> result == (val * gain) / div) && (val >= 4503599627370495 ==> result == (val / div) * gain); */
note: second pass confirms the strict < against GENMASK_ULL(51,0) in rohm-bu27034.c gain_mul_div_helper. Prose and contract kept.

name: bu27034_fixp_calc_t1_64bit
prose: Precondition: ch0 is nonzero and H = gain1 * gain1, computed in unsigned int arithmetic (mod 2^32), is nonzero. Postcondition: with P = (u64)coeff * ch1 * ch1 (mod 2^64): if H > ch0 it returns gain_mul_div_helper(P / H, gain0, ch0), otherwise gain_mul_div_helper(P / ch0, gain0, H), where gain_mul_div_helper multiplies before dividing when its first argument is below 2^52 - 1 and divides before multiplying otherwise. It has no side effects.
note: rohm-bu27034.c:635-655; prose kept after second pass (the branch on helper > ch0 and the division arguments match).

name: bu27034_fixp_calc_t1
prose: Precondition: ch0 and H = gain1 * gain1 (mod 2^32) are nonzero. Postcondition: with S = ch1 * ch1 (32-bit unsigned), if S * coeff overflows 32 bits or (S * coeff) * gain0 overflows 32 bits (checked with check_mul_overflow) it returns bu27034_fixp_calc_t1_64bit(coeff, ch0, ch1, gain0, gain1); otherwise it returns ((S * coeff * gain0) / H) / ch0 using 32-bit unsigned floor divisions, widened to u64. It has no side effects (the first products it computes at the top of the function are overwritten and unused).
note: rohm-bu27034.c:657-676; prose kept after second pass, with the dead initial computations noted.

name: bu27034_fixp_calc_lx
prose: Precondition: when coeff_idx is 0 or 1, ch0 and gain0 are nonzero, gain1 * gain1 (mod 2^32) is nonzero, and 1 <= meastime <= 429496729 (so meastime * 10 does not wrap and is nonzero). Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if coeff_idx is not below the table size 2 (a negative coeff_idx also converts to a large unsigned value and returns -EINVAL). Otherwise it computes terms t0 = bu27034_fixp_calc_t1(A, ch0, ch1, gain0, gain1), t1 = bu27034_fixp_calc_t23(B, ch1, gain1) and t2 = bu27034_fixp_calc_t23(C, ch0, gain0) from the selected coefficient row, sums the terms not marked negative (only A of row 0 is negative), returns 0 if that sum is 0 or if a negative term is greater than or equal to the running result, and otherwise returns (int)((sum - negative terms) / (meastime * 10)) as the u64 quotient truncated to int. It has no side effects.
note: rohm-bu27034.c:698-760; coeff_idx check is coeff_idx >= ARRAY_SIZE(coeff), so any index of 2 or more (and negatives) gives -EINVAL, not only 2.

name: stk3310_check_chip_id
prose: Precondition: none; chip_id may be any u8. Postcondition: it scans stk3310_chip_ids (0x31, 0x13, 0x15, 0x1E, 0x12, 0x1D, 0x51, the ids of the STK3013, STK3310, STK3311A, STK3311S34, STK3311X, STK3311 and STK3335) and returns 0 if chip_id equals one of them, otherwise -ENODEV. It has no side effects.
note: stk3310.c:38-44, 85-93, 214-222. Table checked against the CHIP_ID_VAL defines; contract dropped (mechanical ENODEV check kept failing).

name: ad2s1210_single_conversion
prose: Precondition: the caller does not hold st->lock (it is taken inside with guard(mutex) and dropped on every return), indio_dev and chan are valid and val is writable. Postcondition: it toggles the sample line, takes a timestamp and overwrites st->sample, before any validation of chan->type. In MOD_CONFIG mode it reads the position (IIO_ANGL) or velocity (IIO_ANGL_VEL) bytes with regmap_bulk_read and the fault register with regmap_read, returning -EINVAL for any other channel type and the negative errno of a failing read; in other modes it calls ad2s1210_set_mode (MOD_POS or MOD_VEL, -EINVAL for any other channel type, negative errno on failure) and spi_read of 3 bytes into st->sample (negative errno on failure). On success it sets *val to be16_to_cpu of st->sample.raw (IIO_ANGL) or its sign-extended 16-bit value (IIO_ANGL_VEL), calls ad2s1210_push_events with st->sample.fault and the timestamp, and returns IIO_VAL_INT. On every error return *val is left unmodified and no events are pushed.
note: reviewer (round 15) is wrong: ad2s1210_push_events is called at the end of ad2s1210_single_conversion after the final switch; round 2's missing set_mode errno is already in the prose. Added side effects before the type check.

name: ltc2983_rtd_new
prose: Precondition: child is the firmware node of an RTD channel, st is an initialised ltc2983_data, and sensor has chan and type set. Postcondition: it returns &rtd->sensor for a devm-allocated ltc2983_rtd (owned by the device, not to be freed by the caller) on success, with sensor_config, r_sense_chan, custom (for LTC2983_SENSOR_RTD_CUSTOM), fault_handler, assign_chan, excitation_current and, when adi,rtd-curve is readable, rtd_curve filled in; excitation_current is 1 (5 uA) when adi,excitation-current-microamp cannot be read. The reference to the rsense node is released automatically on every path. It returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) if the allocation fails, an error pointer from fwnode_find_reference if adi,rsense-handle is missing or invalid, the error from reading the rsense node's reg property, and ERR_PTR(-EINVAL) for: adi,number-of-wires present but not 2 to 5; adi,rsense-share with adi,current-rotate while n_wires is 2 or 3 (including the default of 2 wires); a 4-wire configuration with Kelvin rsense and r_sense_chan <= LTC2983_DIFFERENTIAL_CHAN_MIN; a 4-wire configuration with sensor->chan below LTC2983_DIFFERENTIAL_CHAN_MIN or above max_channels_nr (max_channels_nr - 1 with rotation); a non-4-wire configuration with sensor->chan below LTC2983_DIFFERENTIAL_CHAN_MIN (no upper-bound check); or an unsupported excitation current value. It returns ERR_CAST of the error when __ltc2983_custom_sensor_new fails for a custom RTD.
note: reviewer (round 15) is right: the upper channel bound is checked only in the 4-wire branch (the 4-wire branch tests sensor->chan > max, the else branch only tests chan < LTC2983_DIFFERENTIAL_CHAN_MIN); old prose applied it to all. Slice cut the head (name outside slice, function starts at ltc2983.c:737). Added that the rotation check applies when n_wires keeps its default of 2.

name: mlx90632_read_raw
prose: Precondition: indio_dev has private data with an initialised mlx90632_data, channel is valid, val and val2 are writable, and for IIO_CHAN_INFO_SAMP_FREQ the refresh rate index returned by mlx90632_get_refresh_rate is a valid index of mlx90632_freqs. Postcondition: it calls pm_runtime_get_sync and ignores its result, then mlx90632_pm_interraction_wakeup, which switches to continuous mode when the previous interaction was recent and the device is in sleep-step mode and otherwise updates data->interaction_ts to jiffies (it does not update it when it fails); a negative result jumps to the exit. Then for IIO_CHAN_INFO_PROCESSED it returns IIO_VAL_INT with *val from mlx90632_calc_ambient_dsp105 or mlx90632_calc_object_dsp105 (selected by channel2 IIO_MOD_TEMP_AMBIENT or IIO_MOD_TEMP_OBJECT), the negative errno of those calculations if they fail, or -EINVAL for any other channel2; for IIO_CHAN_INFO_CALIBEMISSIVITY it returns IIO_VAL_INT_PLUS_MICRO with 1 and 0 when data->emissivity is 1000, else 0 and data->emissivity * 1000; for IIO_CHAN_INFO_CALIBAMBIENT it returns IIO_VAL_INT with data->object_ambient_temperature; for IIO_CHAN_INFO_SAMP_FREQ it returns IIO_VAL_INT_PLUS_MICRO with the table entry or the negative errno of mlx90632_get_refresh_rate; any other mask gives -EINVAL. Every path after the wakeup call, including the wakeup failure, ends with pm_runtime_put_autosuspend.
note: reviewer (round 15) is right: the PROCESSED path can return negative errnos from the calc functions (mlx90632_read_raw, PROCESSED case); old prose said only IIO_VAL_INT or -EINVAL there. wakeup behaviour checked at mlx90632.c:961-980.

name: ib_cm_init
prose: Precondition: none; module init function. Postcondition: it initialises the cm global's device list, locks, service and remote tables, local-id table and timewait list and a random id operand, then allocates the ib_cm workqueue; if alloc_workqueue fails it returns -ENOMEM with no workqueue or client registered. Otherwise it calls ib_register_client(&cm_client): on failure it destroys the workqueue and returns that negative error; on success it returns 0 with cm.wq allocated and cm_client registered.
note: cm.c:4508-4533; reviewer comments were only about the contract (dropped, global state).

name: cma_port_from_service_id
prose: Precondition: none; service_id is a __be64 value. Postcondition: it returns (u16)be64_to_cpu(service_id), the low 16 bits of the CPU-order value: on a big-endian host these are the low 16 bits of the stored value unchanged, on a little-endian host they are the byte-swapped top 16 bits of the stored 64-bit value (the last two bytes in network order). It has no side effects.
note: reviewers rounds 1 and 15 right: old prose said 'byte-swapped low 16 bits of service_id' on little-endian, but bswap64 followed by truncation gives the byte-swapped HIGH 16 bits (cma.c:1496-1499).
